name: AI share of a task (observed use)
unit: percent 0-100, with low and high reading
method: platform observation: Claude.ai conversations mapped to O*NET tasks
limitations: One AI product's consumer use; no enterprise API, no robots or machines; two months is not a trend
transformation: mean of Anthropic task coverage and (automation x 1 + augmentation x 0.5) for tasks with at least 0.01% of use (scripts/ai_exposure.py)

name: AI share of an occupation's tasks (observed use)
method: platform observation aggregated over the occupation's O*NET tasks
limitations: Thinly used occupations lean on Anthropic's observed exposure or their field, with a wider range
transformation: importance-weighted mean of task shares; thin evidence widens the range (scripts/ai_exposure.py)

name: Hands-off share of a skill or tool
method: platform observation: share of conversations where the whole task is handed over
limitations: Our crosswalk links tools to AI-use topics (data/skill_topic_map.csv); skills inherit their work activities
transformation: automation share of the linked topics or work activities (scripts/ai_exposure.py)

name: GenAI exposure of an ISCO-08 task (technical potential)
method: expert judgement, worker survey and two LLM predictions, reconciled by experts for 46 tasks
limitations: Potential, not use and not job loss; ISCO tasks, not O*NET tasks

name: GenAI exposure gradient of an occupation (technical potential)
unit: mean and SD of task scores 0-1; gradient 1-4, minimal or not exposed
method: ILO's Table 5 rules on the occupation's task mean and SD
limitations: Reaches an O*NET occupation through its ISCO-08 unit group (ESCO crosswalk), so O*NET occupations in one group share a score
transformation: none for the score; mapping basis (exact / close / broad) is shown next to it

name: Share of Malaysia's online job ads by MASCO major group
unit: percent of all ads; change in percentage
source_name: DOSM Big Data Analytics: Job Market Insights
method: count of online job ads on job platforms
limitations: Ads are not hires and not employment; duplicates and platform coverage vary; series breaks in 2025 Q3
transformation: share change of the last two quarters against the two before (scripts/demand.py)

name: MyCOL 2024/2025 critical-occupation status
method: employer surveys and policy review by TalentCorp (66 occupations)
limitations: A list of critical occupations, not a ranking of all occupations
transformation: exact or close ISCO match = yes; broad match or same minor group = near (data/mycol_map.csv)

name: Median monthly wage of a MASCO major group
method: household or establishment survey published by DOSM
limitations: A whole major group, not the occupation; shown as context, never used to rank

name: Pace of AI research
method: count of AI papers in the last 6 months against the 6 before
limitations: Papers are not adoption; all papers grew too

name: Malaysian demand index
method: confidence-weighted mean of MyCOL status and the job-ad share change
limitations: Few signals; a major group stands in for the occupation

name: Speed of AI adoption to 2030
method: an assumption you pick: slow 10%; moderate 25%; fast 50%; or the slider
limitations: An assumption: not a forecast and never shown as one

name: Occupation outlook to 2030 under a scenario
method: demand moved by adoption x tempo x (builder and exposure terms)
limitations: Moves demand between occupations; says nothing about total hiring; not back-tested

name: Stress-test pressure on a task
geography: global potential applied to the occupation
taxonomy: O*NET task with ILO occupation score
method: observed AI share moved towards the ILO potential by adoption x (1 - friction), weighted by task importance
limitations: Engineering proposal, not a published formula; ILO potential is occupation-level here
transformation: pressure = observed + effective adoption x max(0; ILO potential - observed) (scripts/stress_test.py)

name: Skill coverage of a target occupation
method: importance-weighted share of the target's O*NET skills and knowledge the person has at the needed level
limitations: O*NET levels describe US occupations; your levels may come from a self-rating

name: Evidence grade A/B/C
method: three rule-based checks of 0-2 points each
limitations: A grade, not a probability; not calibrated against outcomes

name: Course hours
method: the length the provider states
limitations: Stated length, not time to mastery

name: Your skill level (skills check)
method: self-rating against O*NET's own level examples
limitations: Self-ratings can be off in either direction

name: Your skill evidence from a CV
method: word match of tools and job titles
limitations: Finds what the CV names; misses what it words differently

name: Skills assumed from the job you do now
source_name: O*NET level of your current job
method: doing a job counts as having its O*NET levels
limitations: An assumption: the job's typical level, not yours

name: Skill evidence from a finished mission
source_name: Missions you marked done (with your own evidence)
method: a finished practice task with a product you can show
limitations: We do not check the work; the evidence link is yours
transformation: mission level as a floor for its skills (scripts/missions.py)
